features.label: Why Backupino
features.title: Engineered for real-world hosting
features.subtitle: Every engine inside Backupino was designed to survive the constraints of budget shared hosting — strict 30-second execution limits, tight memory caps, and locked-down system binaries.

items.title: Resumable Anti-Timeout Engine
items.desc: Heavy jobs are sliced into incremental micro-batches with persistent checkpoints in wp_backupino_jobs. After a 504 error or a closed tab, the engine resumes from the exact file or database row.

items.title: Standalone Installer
items.desc: An ultra-lightweight (~80 KB) installer.php is packaged with every archive and rebuilds your entire site on an empty server — no pre-installed WordPress, database or plugin required.

items.title: Pure PHP SQL Streamer
items.desc: Databases are dumped row-by-row through native PDO / MySQLi — no mysqldump, no exec(), no shell access. UTF-8 slugs, 4-byte emojis and serialized data stay 100% intact.

items.title: Permanent Download Link
items.desc: One static URL always resolves to your newest backup — guarded by a 32-byte secret key, administrator authentication and HTTP 429 brute-force rate limiting.

items.title: Telegram & Bale Alerts
items.desc: Instant completion reports with archive size, file count, execution time and a direct download link — delivered directly from your host with a built-in retry queue.

items.title: 100% Offline-First
items.desc: Zero remote scripts, zero CDN calls, zero external fonts, zero telemetry. Completely safe for intranets, firewalled environments and air-gapped systems.

items.q: Does the free version impose size limits or file-count quotas?
items.a: No, absolutely not. Backupino imposes no artificial size limits (such as 2 MB or 512 MB) and no restrictions on the number of files or database records. It runs reliably and without paywalls for everything from small business websites to massive, product-heavy WooCommerce stores.

items.q: Is there any charge for restoring or migrating a package?
items.a: No — restore and site cloning are 100% free forever. Ending the unfair business model of free exports with paid restores was one of the primary motivations behind creating Backupino.

items.q: Do I need WordPress pre-installed on the destination host?
items.a: No. installer.php is a standalone, lightweight, self-contained script. Place it alongside your backup ZIP in a completely empty directory and run it — it extracts files, sets up the database and generates wp-config.php entirely from scratch.

items.q: Is Backupino compatible with WooCommerce stores?
items.a: Yes, 100% compatible. Orders, customer accounts, product metadata and custom WooCommerce database tables are packaged and restored flawlessly without data loss.

items.q: Will disk space fill up if a backup is cancelled or interrupted?
items.a: No. Backupino ships with a Zero-Leftover Guarantee: all temporary files in the jobs/ directory are immediately purged when a job completes or is cancelled.

items.q: Does the plugin send telemetry or analytics to external servers?
items.a: No, never. Backupino is engineered on a 100% offline-first architecture — no telemetry, email addresses, database statistics or analytics are sent to any remote server without your explicit consent.

items.q: Can the permanent download link secret token be brute-forced?
items.a: No. The token is a cryptographically secure 32-byte string compared with the timing-attack-safe hash_equals() function, and the built-in rate limiter blocks IPs for 10 minutes after 5 failed attempts, returning HTTP 429.

why.label: Why We Built It
why.title: Five legacy problems. One modern platform.
why.subtitle: Legacy backup tools designed years ago routinely suffer from structural limitations. Backupino resolves each one at the engine level.

items.title: Ransomware-style restore paywalls
items.desc: Many plugins let you export for free, then block you at the critical moment with 'maximum import size' errors, forcing $69–$99 extensions just to restore your own data. In Backupino, restore and migration are 100% free forever — no artificial file-size caps, multi-gigabyte sites included.

items.title: 504 timeouts on shared hosting
items.desc: Budget hosts enforce 30–60 second execution limits and 128–256 MB RAM caps; single-pass archivers crash hard. Backupino's resumable chunk-based engine processes controlled, multi-megabyte chunks across successive ticks and resumes precisely where it left off.

items.title: Corrupted Unicode slugs & data
items.desc: Single-byte string math breaks serialized arrays, Elementor layouts and non-Latin post slugs during migration. Backupino's deep search-and-replace engine natively handles multibyte encodings, nested serialized objects and JSON strings — guaranteeing 100% data integrity.

items.title: Forced WordPress pre-install
items.desc: Conventional workflows demand a database, a fresh WordPress and the plugin installed on the destination before you can even import. Backupino's standalone installer.php needs only an empty directory — it rebuilds everything from zero.

items.title: No native calendars or messengers
items.desc: Standard tools rely on email that lands in spam, and ignore the Jalali calendar entirely. Backupino ships with both Gregorian and Solar Hijri (Jalali) scheduling plus instant Telegram and Bale notifications with direct download links.

items.q: How are domains counted?
items.a: Licenses bind to your site's home_url. Each unique home_url consumes one domain seat on your plan.

items.q: Subdomains and Multisite
items.a: Every subdomain counts as a separate domain. A WordPress Multisite network — no matter how many subsites — counts as a single domain.

items.q: Local & test environments
items.a: localhost, .test, .local, .dev domains and raw IP addresses are fully excluded and never consume a seat.

items.q: Staging exemptions
items.a: Up to 2 staging environments per license are exempt, so you can test restores safely before production.

items.q: Domain release cooldown
items.a: Released domains carry a 72-hour cooldown before the seat can be reassigned to a new domain.

items.q: Renewal reminders & grace
items.a: You are notified 3 days before expiry, followed by a 7-day grace period. Afterwards Pro features pause while read access to existing backups is preserved.

items.q: Yearly activation caps
items.a: Freelancer offers unlimited domain changes with a 30 activations/year cap; Enterprise offers unlimited changes with a 100 activations/year cap.

items.q: How are domains counted?
items.a: By home_url: every subdomain counts as a separate domain, an entire Multisite network counts as one, and local/test addresses (localhost, .test, .local, .dev, raw IPs) are excluded entirely.

items.q: Do staging environments count as domains?
items.a: No. Up to 2 staging environments are exempt on every plan, so you can validate migrations and restores without burning seats.

items.q: What happens after the trial ends?
items.a: The 10-day trial simply ends — Pro features pause and you keep full access to your existing backups. Choose any plan to continue with Pro, or stay on the free core forever.

items.q: Can I upgrade my plan later?
items.a: Yes. Upgrade directly from your account panel — your license, connected domains and all settings carry over instantly.

items.q: What happens when my license expires?
items.a: Renewal reminders arrive 3 days before expiry, followed by a 7-day grace period. After grace, Pro features pause while read access to every existing backup is preserved.

items.q: Is the dedicated cloud available on all plans?
items.a: Backupino Dedicated Cloud ships with Freelancer (30 GB, 5 versions) and Enterprise (100 GB, 10 versions), with quota alerts at 80% and 100% and automatic retention policies.

items.q: What is the yearly activation cap?
items.a: Personal allows 2 domain changes per year. Freelancer allows unlimited changes within 30 activations/year, and Enterprise within 100 activations/year — plenty of headroom for rotating client work.

hero.label: Privacy Policy
hero.title: Your data never leaves your server
hero.subtitle: Backupino is engineered on a 100% offline-first, zero-telemetry architecture. This policy explains — precisely and without legalese fog — how your data is handled.

sections.title: Overview
paras: Backupino is an open-source WordPress backup, cloning and migration platform released under the GPL-2.0 license. The plugin executes entirely inside your own hosting environment — it has no centralized cloud service, no account system on our side, and no remote control channel of any kind.

This policy describes what data the plugin handles, where it lives, and the security controls that protect it. The short version: your backups, your database and your configuration remain on your infrastructure at all times.

sections.title: Data We Store
paras: All artifacts produced by Backupino are stored locally on your own server — nothing is synchronized to, mirrored on, or uploaded to any external infrastructure:
If wp-content/ is read-only on restrictive shared hosting, storage automatically and securely falls back to uploads/backupino/ so operations succeed seamlessly — still entirely on your server.
list: Backup archives (.zip) — stored in wp-content/backupino/packages/, hardened against direct web access.
Job state & checkpoints — tracked in the wp_backupino_jobs database table (token, status, stage, progress, payload) so interrupted jobs can resume.
Settings & messenger tokens — stored in the standard wp_options table inside your own WordPress database.
Temporary staging chunks — kept in wp-content/backupino/jobs/ and purged immediately on completion or cancellation (Zero-Garbage Guarantee).

sections.title: Zero Telemetry
paras: Backupino collects nothing. No telemetry data, email addresses, database statistics or analytics are transmitted to any remote server without your explicit consent — and the plugin contains no routine that does so implicitly.

All CSS files, JavaScript bundles, fonts and icons are bundled locally within the plugin package. The plugin never requests external CDNs that could be blocked, censored or throttled by regional networks or firewalls, ensuring full compatibility in restricted intranet and national network environments.

sections.title: Archive Protection
paras: Backup archives are stored in wp-content/backupino/packages/. This path is automatically hardened by multiple strict security layers:
list: An .htaccess file configured with Options -Indexes and Require all denied — completely blocking HTTP requests and directory browsing on Apache and LiteSpeed.
A dedicated web.config file for Windows and IIS servers.
Execution blocking for all executable extensions (.php, .py, .cgi, etc.) inside the backup directory — preventing remote code execution even if unauthorized server access occurs.
A blank index.php file preventing directory listing fallthrough.

Every plugin PHP source file enforces defined( 'ABSPATH' ) || exit;, so direct browser requests terminate immediately with a blank response; installer components are guarded by defined( 'BACKUPINO_INSTALLER' ).

sections.title: Download-Link Security
paras: The permanent latest-backup download link is protected by a multi-layer security architecture designed against unauthorized data exfiltration:
list: High-entropy 32-byte secret key — generated cryptographically and verified with PHP's constant-time hash_equals() comparison to defeat timing-attack side channels.
Brute-force rate limiting — 5 consecutive failed attempts trigger an automatic 10-minute IP block, returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.
Mandatory administrator session validation — guest requests are redirected to wp-login.php, and authenticated users lacking the manage_options capability receive HTTP 403 Forbidden.
Instant key regeneration — rotating the token in settings invalidates the previous download URL immediately.

sections.title: API & CSRF Protection
paras: All sensitive AJAX and REST API endpoints verify WordPress administrator capabilities (manage_options) and validate standard WordPress security nonces (X-WP-Nonce: wp_rest) to eliminate Cross-Site Request Forgery vectors.
Direct invocation of the plugin's PHP source files via a browser is impossible: every file enforces a strict ABSPATH guard clause and terminates direct web requests immediately.

sections.title: Integrations & Tokens
paras: Telegram and Bale bot tokens are securely stored in the WordPress database (wp_options). They are never printed in public debug logs and never exposed in API responses.

Tokens are strictly transmitted as authorization headers directly to the messaging provider's official API during notification dispatch. Messages travel directly from your host to Telegram or Bale servers — no intermediate or centralized third-party server is involved.
Whenever you disable a notification channel, the saved token and Chat ID remain stored but no network request is dispatched. Deleting the values removes them permanently from your database.

sections.title: Third-Party Services
paras: This website links to external platforms that operate under their own privacy policies — GitHub (source code, documentation and issue tracking), WordPress.org (plugin directory profile), Telegram and Bale (optional notification delivery you configure yourself).

The account and registration features on this website are provided for product access demonstration. Any information you enter in these forms is processed locally in your browser for validation and is not transmitted to, or stored on, any Backupino server.

sections.title: Changes to This Policy
paras: We revise this policy alongside notable plugin releases. All documentation and releases follow Backupino's custom Major.Minor.Patch versioning specification, and material policy changes are announced through the project's GitHub repositories prior to release.
Continued use of the plugin after an update constitutes acceptance of the revised policy. The current revision of this policy dates to November 2026.

sections.title: Contact Us
paras: Questions about this policy, a security disclosure, or a data-handling concern? Open an issue on the plugin's GitHub tracker or reach us through the official WordPress.org profile — security reports are triaged with priority.
Plugin repository: github.com/Backupino/plugin • Documentation repository: github.com/Backupino/documents • WordPress.org profile: profiles.wordpress.org/backupino

what-is.title: What is Backupino?
what-is.intro: Backupino is a modern, resumable and self-contained WordPress backup, cloning and easy migration platform — engineered for real-world shared hosting and 100% offline-first operation.

blocks.text: Every backup is packaged as a standard .zip archive plus an ultra-lightweight standalone installer (installer.php, ~80 KB) that rebuilds your entire site on an empty server — no pre-installed WordPress required. A resumable chunk engine keeps multi-gigabyte jobs alive inside strict 30-second execution limits.
Core pillars

items: Truly free — backup, restore and migration with no artificial size limits, forever.
Resumable processing — micro-batches with persistent checkpoints survive 504 timeouts and closed tabs.
Zero-dependency restore — the standalone installer rebuilds files, database and wp-config.php from an empty directory.
Offline-first & private — no CDNs, no remote scripts, no telemetry. Safe for intranets and air-gapped systems.

blocks.text: Tip: everything in this handbook applies to the free core. Capabilities marked with a PRO badge are provided by the Backupino Pro companion plugin.

free-vs-pro.title: Free vs Pro Overview
free-vs-pro.intro: Backupino ships in two editions that work together: the GPL-2.0 free core, and the Pro companion plugin that layers professional tooling on top.

blocks.text: The free core (forever free)

items: Unlimited full, database-only and files-only backups with exclusion rules.
Standalone installer.php migration to any host or domain, with deep serialized + JSON URL replacement.
Monthly scheduling with Jalali & Gregorian calendars, and personal Telegram / Bale bot notifications.
Pure PHP SQL streamer, resumable chunk engine, permanent download link and WP-CLI commands.

blocks.text: The Pro layer (companion plugin)

items: Cloud destinations — S3-compatible services, Google Drive, Dropbox, FTP/FTPS/SFTP download hosts.
Incremental backup chains with point-in-time restore, and secure in-place restore with preview + rollback.
Advanced scheduling (hourly → custom) with automated create → transfer → clean chains.
Encryption (AES-256-GCM, XChaCha), Multisite, teams, white label, central panel and Backupino Dedicated Cloud.

blocks.text: Backupino Pro requires the free plugin installed and active. It extends the core — it never replaces it, and nothing that is free ever moves behind a paywall.

system-requirements.title: System Requirements
system-requirements.intro: Backupino is engineered to operate efficiently with minimal server resources — no external binaries, no privileged system access.

items: Required extensions: pdo_mysql or mysqli, json, and zip (with an internal PclZip fallback).
Recommended extensions: mbstring (multibyte-safe search & replace), openssl (HTTPS dispatch), curl (reliable core HTTP requests).
Verified stacks: Apache 2.4+, LiteSpeed/OpenLiteSpeed, Nginx + PHP-FPM, Microsoft IIS — with cPanel & WHM, DirectAdmin, Plesk, CyberPanel, Cloudways and RunCloud.

blocks.text: wp-content/ needs standard write permissions — 755 for directories and 644 for files. The internal wp-content/backupino/ storage directory is created automatically with a hardened .htaccess (Deny from all) and a blank index.php that prevents directory listing.

install-free.title: Installation (Free)
install-free.intro: Four supported installation paths — from one-click directory install to fully automated WP-CLI deployment.

items: WordPress directory (recommended): Plugins → Add New, search for Backupino, Install Now, then Activate.
ZIP upload: download the latest release package from GitHub, then Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin → Install Now → Activate.
Manual FTP / file manager: upload the extracted backupino directory into wp-content/plugins/ and activate it under Plugins → Installed Plugins.
WP-CLI: ideal for headless servers and CI/CD pipelines — see the command below.

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
# Install and activate from the WordPress directory:
wp plugin install backupino --activate

# Or from a local zip package:
wp plugin install /path/to/backupino.zip --activate

# Verify installation status and system health:
wp backupino status

blocks.text: After activation open Backupino → Settings → System Status and confirm every prerequisite indicator (PHP version, PDO/Zip extensions, storage write permissions) shows a green Pass checkmark.

install-pro.title: Installation (Pro — Companion Plugin)
install-pro.intro: Backupino Pro installs alongside the free core and activates with your license key. The free plugin must be installed and active first.

items: Log in to your Backupino account panel and download the Pro package (backupino-pro.zip).
In wp-admin open Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose the package, Install Now, then Activate.
Open Backupino → License, paste your license key, and click Activate License — the key binds to this site's home_url.
A confirmation banner appears and the Pro tabs (Cloud, Scheduling, Restore, Team) become available in the dashboard.

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
# Pro installation via WP-CLI:
wp plugin install /path/to/backupino-pro.zip --activate

# Then activate the license from the account panel CLI:
wp backupino license activate --key="BKN-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX"

blocks.text: Local and staging environments (localhost, .test, .local, .dev, raw IPs) never consume a domain seat — activate Pro there freely for testing.

general-settings.title: General Settings
general-settings.intro: The Backupino dashboard organizes every control into task-focused tabs inside wp-admin.

items: Dashboard — one-click Create Backup, live progress card with stage percentages and instant Cancel.
Backups — package inventory with labels, sizes, dates, download and delete actions.
Settings → System Status — environment checks for PHP, extensions and write permissions.
Settings → Archive & Exclusions — exclusion patterns, size thresholds and batch size.
Settings → Scheduling and Notifications — automation intervals plus Telegram / Bale toggles.
Settings → Download Link — your permanent latest-backup URL and secret key rotation.
Pro tabs — Cloud destinations, Advanced Scheduling, In-Place Restore, License and Team (when Pro is active).

blocks.text: Every settings change saves instantly with a confirmation toast, and sensitive actions (rotation, deletion, restore) always require explicit confirmation. The interface ships fully translated for Persian sites with native Shamsi date display.

backup-scope.title: Backup Scope (Files, Database, Full)
backup-scope.intro: Choose exactly what goes into each package — full site, database-only, or files-only.

items: Full Backup — all WordPress files (themes, plugins, uploads, core) plus the database and the standalone installer.php. Best for migration and disaster recovery.
Database Only — an ultra-fast, lightweight SQL package. Ideal before publishing content, adjusting settings or running minor updates.
Files Only — media, code and asset packages without the database dump. Ideal before theme or plugin changes.

blocks.text: Scope selection lives on the dashboard's Create Backup card and in WP-CLI via dedicated flags, so routine operations stay one click — or one command — away.

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
wp backupino create              # full backup
wp backupino create --db-only    # database only
wp backupino create --files-only # files only

exclusions.title: Exclusion Rules
exclusions.intro: Trim heavy media folders, logs and development directories out of your archives with pattern-based exclusion rules.

blocks.text: In Settings → Archive & Exclusions, add one rule per line. Directory rules (wp-content/uploads/videos/), glob patterns (*.mp4, *.zip, *.iso, *.tar.gz, node_modules/) and diagnostic logs (debug.log, error_log) are all supported. The engine always auto-excludes its own backupino/ storage directory and transient cache folders.

items: Skip Files Larger Than (MB) — bypass individual files above a threshold such as 50 or 100; set 0 for unlimited.
Batch File Processing — files handled per execution tick; default 300, lower to 100 on constrained hosts or raise to 1000 on dedicated servers.

blocks.text: Excluding core WordPress files (wp-admin, wp-includes) breaks standalone restores. Limit rules to uploads, caches, logs and large media or development folders.

local-storage.title: Local Storage Settings
local-storage.intro: Every artifact Backupino produces lives on your own server — hardened against direct web access.

items: wp-content/backupino/packages/ — finalized .zip archives plus their matching installer.php files.
wp-content/backupino/jobs/ — transient staging chunks, split SQL dumps and runtime logs (purged immediately on completion or cancellation).
Storage hardening — an .htaccess with Options -Indexes and Require all denied, a web.config for IIS, execution blocking for .php/.py/.cgi and a blank index.php.

blocks.text: Read-only wp-content? Backupino automatically and securely falls back to uploads/backupino/ so backups keep succeeding on restrictive shared hosting.

retention.title: Version Retention (1–100)
retention.intro: Local version management keeps between 1 and 100 recent archives on your host and prunes the rest automatically.

blocks.text: Set the retention count in Settings → Backups (default: 3). After each successful backup, Backupino inspects the package inventory — when the count exceeds your threshold, the oldest archive, its metadata records and its matching installer files are safely and permanently pruned from disk. This guarantee holds for manual, scheduled and CLI-created backups alike.

items: Range: 1–100 retained versions (Pro adds policy-driven rules such as keep-daily-for-N-weeks).
Pinned packages are never pruned — pin a milestone archive to keep it indefinitely.
Pruning prevents Disk Full errors and hosting suspensions caused by archive accumulation.

download-link.title: Permanent Download Link
download-link.intro: One static URL always resolves to your newest verified backup package — the backbone of off-site automation.

items: High-entropy 32-byte secret key, compared with the timing-attack-safe hash_equals() function.
Brute-force rate limiting: 5 consecutive failures trigger a 10-minute IP block (HTTP 429).
Mandatory administrator session: guests redirect to wp-login.php; non-admins receive HTTP 403.
Instant key regeneration from settings whenever you suspect compromise.

blocks.title: cURL example
blocks.content:
# Automated off-site pull using an authenticated admin cookie:
curl -b "wordpress_cookie.txt" -L -o "latest-backup.zip" \
  "https://yourdomain.com/?backupino_download=latest&backupino_key=YOUR_SECRET_KEY"

notifications.title: Notification Setup (Telegram & Bale)
notifications.intro: Personal bots deliver instant completion reports — archive size, file count, execution time and a direct download link — straight from your host.

items: Telegram: create a bot with the verified @BotFather (/newbot), copy the HTTP API token, then start your bot and read your numeric Chat ID from @userinfobot.
Backupino → Settings → Notifications: enable Telegram, paste the Bot Token and Chat ID, Save, then Send Test Message.
Bale: register a bot in Bale's bot creator, copy the token, and toggle Bale on — Telegram and Bale switches are fully independent.
Messages are dispatched directly from your host to the provider's API with a built-in retry queue for momentary network interruptions.

blocks.text: Tokens are stored in wp_options, never printed in logs, and are sent strictly as authorization headers to the messaging provider during dispatch.

persian-calendar.title: Persian & Shamsi Calendar
persian-calendar.intro: Backupino is calendar-aware: Persian sites schedule and timestamp everything against the Solar Hijri (Jalali) calendar natively.

items: fa_IR sites — automated monthly runs target the 1st day of every Jalali solar month (1 Farvardin, 1 Ordibehesht, 1 Khordad…) at 00:00 midnight.
International sites — execution triggers at 00:00 on the first day of each Gregorian month.
Leap years and variable month lengths (31/30/29 days) resolve through pure mathematical conversion — zero external calendar dependencies.
Reports, notifications and backup labels render dates in the site's native calendar automatically.

monthly-free.title: Monthly Schedule (Free)
monthly-free.intro: The free core automates a monthly backup using WordPress's native wp_cron subsystem — no server cron needed.

items: Open Backupino → Settings → Scheduling.
Toggle Enable Automatic Backups.
Choose Monthly in the interval selection.
Save Changes — the job fires at 00:00 on the first day of the month (Jalali or Gregorian, per site locale).

blocks.text: wp_cron depends on site traffic. On very quiet sites, pair a real system cron with the heartbeat endpoint — see the WP-Cron guide in Troubleshooting.

advanced-pro.title: Advanced Scheduling (Pro)
advanced-pro.intro: Pro turns scheduling into a precision instrument: intervals from hourly to fully custom, chained with remote transfer and local cleanup.

blocks.text: Intervals: hourly to custom

Choose Hourly, Twice Daily, Daily, Weekly or a fully custom interval defined in hours. The scheduler aligns runs to your site's change frequency — high-velocity WooCommerce stores run hourly deltas, while brochure sites settle for weekly runs. Execution state checkpoints between every tick, so no interval ever overlaps or double-fires.
The automated backup chain

Each scheduled run executes a deterministic chain: create the backup locally, transfer it to every configured remote destination (cloud and/or download host), then clean local copies according to your retention policy. A run only marks success after every transfer verifies its checksum, and failures enter the retry queue with Telegram / Bale or Central Bot reporting.

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
# Configure an hourly chained schedule from the CLI:
wp backupino schedule set --interval=hourly --chain=cloud,clean

cloud-overview.title: Cloud Storage Overview
cloud-overview.intro: Pro streams every finished package to storage you own — destinations never see your WordPress credentials.

items: S3-compatible services — Amazon S3, ArvanCloud, Liara, ParsPack, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, Backblaze B2.
Google Drive and Dropbox with OAuth connections and folder targeting.
Download hosts over FTP, FTPS and SFTP with automatic per-domain folders.

blocks.text: Enable Keep local copy to retain the newest archive on the host alongside cloud copies, or disable it for a strictly off-site flow. Every transfer verifies integrity before the job closes, and the report carries per-destination success states.

Your cloud keys stay with you: Pro uses your own buckets and accounts — there is no intermediary storage you do not control (except the optional Backupino Dedicated Cloud on Freelancer and Enterprise).

s3.title: S3-Compatible Services
s3.intro: Any S3-compatible object store connects with an endpoint, region, bucket, access key and secret. Transfers use multipart upload with per-part verification.

blocks.title: Connection fields
blocks.content:
Endpoint:   https://<provider-endpoint>
Region:     <region-or-auto>
Bucket:     my-site-backups
Access Key: ••••••••
Secret Key: ••••••••
Path style: subdomain/vhost style (default) or path style (MinIO)

blocks.text: Amazon S3

Create a bucket in your preferred region, issue a least-privilege IAM key limited to that bucket, and connect. Versioning and lifecycle rules in the bucket pair naturally with Backupino's version retention.
ArvanCloud
Copy the endpoint from your ArvanCloud object storage panel, create an access key, and point Backupino at the bucket — domestic network routing keeps transfers fast for Iranian hosts.
Liara
Liara's object storage exposes a standard S3 API; paste the endpoint from the Liara console, select the bucket and authenticate with your access key and secret.
ParsPack
ParsPack object storage works identically — endpoint, bucket, key and secret from the hosting panel — giving you another domestic, S3-compatible destination.
MinIO
Self-hosted MinIO is supported with path-style addressing (for example https://minio.internal:9000). Internal DNS names and private networks work without any public exposure.
Cloudflare R2
R2's S3 endpoint (<account_id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com) plus an R2 API token is all you need — zero-egress pricing makes deep backup chains inexpensive.
Wasabi
Point to s3.<region>.wasabisys.com with your Wasabi keys for hot-cloud storage pricing without retrieval fees.
Backblaze B2
Use the B2 S3-compatible endpoint (s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com) with an application key scoped to your backup bucket.
Run Test Connection after saving any S3 destination — the panel lists reachable buckets and confirms write permission before your first scheduled transfer.

google-drive.title: Google Drive
google-drive.intro: Connect Drive with a one-click OAuth flow and stream backups into a folder in your own Google account.

items: Open Backupino → Cloud → Google Drive and click Connect.
Approve access in Google's OAuth window — the token stores locally in wp_options and never appears in logs.
Choose or create the target folder (for example Backups/example.com).
Run Test Upload to verify quota and permissions.

blocks.text: Large packages upload in resumable chunks, so an interrupted transfer continues from the last confirmed chunk instead of restarting. Revoke access any time from either your Backupino panel or your Google account permissions.

dropbox.title: Dropbox
dropbox.intro: Dropbox receives packages into your app folder with chunked uploads and automatic version naming.

items: Open Backupino → Cloud → Dropbox and click Connect to authorize the app.
Pick the destination directory (default: /Backupino/<domain>).
Confirm with Test Upload — a small integrity package uploads and verifies end-to-end.

blocks.text: Dropbox's content-hash verification runs on every upload, so corrupt transfers are impossible to miss. Paired with point-in-time restore, any Drive or Dropbox object becomes a restore source directly from the panel.

download-host.title: Download Host (FTP / FTPS / SFTP)
download-host.intro: Push packages to any file server you control — shared boxes, NAS appliances or a dedicated download host.

blocks.title: Connection fields
blocks.content:
Protocol: FTP | FTPS (explicit TLS) | SFTP (SSH)
Host:     dl.example.com
Port:     21 | 990 | 22
Username: backups
Password / Key: ••••••••
Base path: /backups
Passive mode: recommended behind NAT

blocks.text: Pro creates a per-domain folder structure (<base>/<domain>/<year>/<month>) automatically, so a single download host can serve an entire fleet without collisions. SFTP connections prefer key-based authentication and verify host fingerprints on first contact.
If listings time out behind firewalled hosting, enable Passive mode and restrict the server firewall to your control panel's published ports.

creating-backup.title: Creating a Backup
creating-backup.intro: One click on the dashboard — or one WP-CLI command — produces a self-restoring package in four transparent stages.

items: Open Backupino in the WordPress sidebar and configure Include Files, Include Database and an optional filename label (e.g. pre-update).
Click Create Backup and watch the live progress card.

Stage 1 Scan catalogs the filesystem; Stage 2 Database streams rows through a 256 KB buffer with 250-row batches; Stage 3 Files performs adaptive chunk compression; Stage 4 Finalize seals the archive, verifies the manifest and injects installer.php.
Download the .zip (and installer.php for migration) from the Backups tab.

blocks.text: Switch tabs freely: the Browser Heartbeat (visibilitychange listener) re-synchronizes when you return, and wp_raise_memory_limit('admin') raises memory automatically during the heavy stages.

resumable.title: Resumable Step-by-Step Processing
resumable.intro: The anti-timeout engine slices heavy work into micro-batches tracked by persistent checkpoints — the reason backups finish on 30-second shared hosting.

blocks.text: Files compress in batches (default 300 per execution tick) and SQL streams through 250-row INSERT batches kept beneath max_allowed_packet. Every job records its token, status, stage, progress percentage and a JSON payload with the exact file pointer, table byte offsets and row counters in the wp_backupino_jobs table.

items: Killed request? WP-Cron and asynchronous ticks reload the state and resume at the precise file or database row.
Closed browser tab? Processing continues in the background and the dashboard catches up on your next visit.
Memory spikes? wp_raise_memory_limit('admin') escalates allocation during scan and compression phases.

php-export.title: PHP-Based DB Export
php-export.intro: The Pure PHP SQL Streamer dumps entire databases through native PDO / MySQLi — no mysqldump, no exec(), no shell permissions.

items: Row-by-row streaming into an unbuffered .sql file keeps memory flat regardless of table size.
UTF-8 / UTF8MB4 encodings, 4-byte emojis and non-Latin URL slugs are preserved byte-perfectly — no intermediate string manipulation.
Optimized multi-row INSERTs stay deliberately beneath MySQL's max_allowed_packet for smooth imports.
Views, triggers and custom WooCommerce tables export alongside core tables.

blocks.text: During import, the installer splits oversized INSERTs into micro-statements, recovers from MariaDB tablespace collisions (Error 1813) and sanitizes incompatible DEFINER clauses automatically.

incremental.title: Incremental Backup (Pro)
incremental.intro: After one full base backup, Pro captures only what changed — dramatically smaller transfers, storage use and runtimes.

blocks.text: Base backup
Every chain starts with a complete base package (files + database) anchored by a manifest of cryptographic per-file checksums. The base is the recovery root; all subsequent work references it.
Delta packages

Each scheduled run diffs the live filesystem against the manifest and packages only new, modified and deleted files plus changed database rows. A delta is typically a small fraction of your full size, which makes hourly schedules practical even on busy stores.
Chain management

Chains self-repair: if a delta's checksum fails verification, the next run automatically re-anchors with a fresh base. Chain length policies cap how many deltas can hang off a base before consolidation, and compaction merges aging deltas to keep restore graphs short.
Incremental chains feed Point-in-Time Restore — any snapshot in your history, rebuilt from base + deltas on demand.

managing-versions.title: Managing Backup Versions
managing-versions.intro: The Backups tab is your inventory: inspect, download, pin or prune any package — locally and (with Pro) across every cloud destination.

items: Every package shows its label, size, type, calendar-aware date and live log.
Actions: Download, Download Installer, Pin (exclude from retention pruning) and Delete with confirmation.
Cloud columns (Pro) mirror destination states per package — uploaded, pending or retrying.
Retention interplays cleanly: pruning removes local copies while remote versions follow their own cloud version policy.

installer.title: Standalone Installer (Free)
installer.intro: The ~80 KB installer.php rebuilds your entire site on an empty server — extraction, database, wp-config and URL replacement, no WordPress required.

blocks.text: How it works

Upload your backup .zip and installer.php into the destination's empty web root, then open https://yourdomain.com/installer.php. A 7-step wizard runs entirely on AJAX ticks, so even multi-gigabyte sites restore inside strict shared-hosting limits.
File extraction

Files extract 300 per tick, with automatic quarantine of the source site's .htaccess, .user.ini, php.ini and wp-config.php as .backupino-orig files — eliminating the LiteSpeed/cPanel 500 errors that kill conventional restores mid-flight.
Database import

The SQL dump streams in with packet-size auto-splitting, MariaDB/MySQL 8 error resilience (orphan tablespace recovery), FOREIGN_KEY_CHECKS=0 handling and DEFINER-clause sanitization. Change the table prefix here if you like — user roles and capability keys update automatically.
WordPress configuration

A fresh wp-config.php is generated with cryptographically secure random salts while preserving your custom constants, followed by a standard .htaccess with the exact RewriteBase for the target directory. Custom login slugs from security plugins are detected automatically.
URL replacement (serialized, JSON, nested)

The deep search-and-replace engine rewrites source URLs to the target across every table — recalculating byte lengths inside serialized PHP structures, traversing JSON strings, preserving Elementor dynamic tags (%7B%7D) and keeping Persian/Unicode slugs intact. A final cleanup step purges installer, archive, dump and quarantined files before redirecting to wp-login.php.
Keep both files together: the installer pairs its embedded 32-character token with the archive's SHA-256 hash, so mismatched packages are rejected before any destructive step.

in-place.title: Secure In-Place Restore (Pro)
in-place.intro: Restore directly on your live site through a guarded seven-stage pipeline — every stage verified before the next begins, with rollback one step away.

blocks.text: 1 — Pre-restore snapshot
Before anything changes, Pro captures a complete safety snapshot of the current site (files + database). This snapshot is the guaranteed way home.
2 — Shadow environment
Your selected backup — local, cloud or incremental chain point — is extracted and prepared in an isolated directory. Your live site keeps serving visitors untouched.
3 — Preview & health check
A sandboxed preview loads the restored site. Automated checks verify WordPress boot status, database integrity, admin access and key site settings before anything is applied.
4 — Owner confirmation
Applying changes requires explicit approval: re-authentication plus a one-time code issued to the account owner. Unattended or unauthorized restores cannot proceed.
5 — Apply changes
The verified snapshot deploys to production through a controlled, transactional switch — files swap atomically and the database applies with verified statements.
6 — Post-restore verification
Immediately after deployment, an automated health sweep re-checks boot, database integrity and front-end responses, then reports to your notification channels.
7 — Rollback
If the health sweep — or your own eyes — catch a problem, one action reverts the site to the pre-restore snapshot. Rollback itself is verified the same way.
Owner confirmation is mandatory by design: restores that bypass re-authentication are rejected, and every attempt is audit-logged to the panel.

encryption.title: Backup Encryption (AES-256-GCM, XChaCha)
encryption.intro: Pro encrypts packages client-side before transfer or storage — ciphertext is the only thing that ever leaves your server.

items: AES-256-GCM — authenticated encryption with integrity proofs for every package.
XChaCha — extended-nonce stream encryption available for maximum operational safety.
Encryption happens before upload, so cloud providers, download hosts and networks only ever see ciphertext.
Decryption occurs locally at restore time; no service — including Backupino's own panel — can read your backups.

blocks.text: Your encryption key stays with you. Losing it without a configured Key Recovery layer makes encrypted backups unrecoverable — enable key recovery for mission-critical sites.

key-management.title: Key Management
key-management.intro: Encryption keys generate on your server, stay on your server, and rotate on your schedule.

items: Keys derive with cryptographically secure randomness and store locally, never transmitted in plaintext.
Rotation creates a new active key while older packages remain decryptable through the local key ring.
Restores prompt for the key only when needed and never echo it into logs or API responses.
The panel displays key fingerprints (not keys) so teams can verify they are restoring with the right material.

key-recovery.title: Key Recovery (Shamir 2-of-3)
key-recovery.intro: An optional enterprise-grade layer that guarantees you can never be locked out of your own encrypted backups.

blocks.text: Your encryption key splits into three mathematical shares using Shamir's Secret Sharing. Any two shares reconstruct the key; one share alone reveals nothing.

items: Share 1 stays on your server — day-to-day operation is unchanged.
Share 2 lives in your Backupino account panel, encrypted and unreadable on its own.
Share 3 downloads to you as an offline recovery file — store it somewhere safe.

recovery-agent.title: Standalone Recovery Agent
recovery-agent.intro: A lightweight agent at your site root that executes authorized recovery operations even when WordPress cannot boot.

items: Deployed at the document root and operates independently of the WordPress runtime.
Executes only signed, authorized recovery commands issued from your Backupino panel.
Communicates over authenticated, encrypted channels — unknown or tampered commands are rejected.
Pairs with in-place restore: when wp-admin is unreachable, the agent performs the same guarded pipeline.

blocks.text: The agent accepts nothing it cannot cryptographically verify — command signatures are validated against your license's Ed25519 keys before any action.

storage-protection.title: Local Storage Protection
storage-protection.intro: Backup archives are never web-accessible — multiple hardening layers guard the packages directory on every server type.

items: .htaccess with Options -Indexes and Require all denied for Apache and LiteSpeed.
A dedicated web.config providing equivalent rules on Windows / IIS.
Execution blocking for .php, .py, .cgi and other executable extensions inside the backup directory.
A blank index.php preventing directory listing fallthrough.
Every plugin PHP file enforces defined( 'ABSPATH' ) || exit; and installer components enforce defined( 'BACKUPINO_INSTALLER' ).

central-panel.title: Centralized Panel
central-panel.intro: Your Backupino account panel is mission control: every connected domain, backup and restore — in one place.

items: Request backups and restores remotely without logging into each wp-admin.
Monitor site health, last-backup age and destination states across the whole fleet.
Approve sensitive operations — owner-confirmed restores require panel-side authorization.
Audit history records every command, signature check and outcome.

central-bot.title: Backupino Central Bot
central-bot.intro: One Telegram bot for the entire fleet — unified backup reporting delivered by Backupino's own bot.

blocks.text: The Central Bot complements (not replaces) the free version's personal bot notifications. Activate it from your account panel, link your Telegram account once, and every connected domain reports into a single stream with domain-tagged messages: backup success, transfer verification, quota warnings and restore audits.
Personal bots keep working per-site on the free core; the Central Bot simply aggregates — useful when you manage more than a handful of domains.

dedicated-cloud.title: Backupino Dedicated Cloud
dedicated-cloud.intro: Cloud storage included with your plan — zero third-party accounts required.

blocks.text: Freelancer ships with 30 GB and 5 retained cloud versions; Enterprise ships with 100 GB and 10 versions. Dedicated Cloud behaves like any other destination — chains transfer to it automatically and point-in-time restore reads from it directly.
Quota & alerts
The panel tracks consumption in real time with alerts at 80% and 100% of quota — via the dashboard, email and the Central Bot — so storage never fills silently.
Retention policies

Automatic version management prunes the oldest cloud versions beyond your plan's count; pinned packages are exempt. Local and cloud retention stay independent, so a trimmed cloud never deletes your last local copy.

team-members.title: Team Members
team-members.intro: Collaborate safely: multiple seats per account with centralized license management.

items: Personal includes 1 seat, Freelancer includes 3, Enterprise includes up to 10.
Seats manage domains, destinations and schedules without sharing the owner's credentials.
Sensitive operations (restores, key material, license actions) remain owner-gated with one-time codes.
Seats attach and detach instantly from the panel as client rosters change.

white-label.title: White Label
white-label.intro: Deliver client-facing backups with your agency's brand — not ours.

blocks.text: On selected plans, the Backupino name, menus and report signatures disappear from wp-admin. Clients see a clean, neutral backup screen, and notification templates adopt your wording. White label applies per-domain and toggles per site, so mixed portfolios stay flexible.

license-structure.title: License Structure (Ed25519)
license-structure.intro: Pro licenses are signed documents — cryptographically verifiable offline, impossible to forge.

blocks.text: Each license is a compact JSON document signed with Ed25519. The plugin verifies the signature locally against the published public key, so validation never depends on a remote server being reachable.
Tampered documents fail signature verification instantly — a license cannot be edited into something it is not.

domain-rules.title: Domain Counting Rules
domain-rules.intro: Licenses bind to your site's home_url — with fair, documented edge rules.

items: Each unique home_url consumes one seat on your plan.
Subdomains count as separate domains.
A WordPress Multisite network counts as one domain regardless of subsite count.
Local/test hosts — localhost, .test, .local, .dev and raw IP addresses — never consume a seat.
Up to 2 staging environments per license are exempt.

activation.title: Activation & Deactivation
activation.intro: Move licenses between domains deliberately — with guardrails that prevent seat churn abuse.

items: Activate from Backupino → License by pasting your key; the seat binds to the current home_url.
Deactivate any time from the panel or the plugin to release the seat.
Released domains carry a 72-hour cooldown before the seat can bind elsewhere.
Yearly activation caps: Personal 2 changes/year, Freelancer 30 activations/year, Enterprise 100 activations/year — all with unlimited deactivations.

offline-cache.title: Offline Cache (7-day)
offline-cache.intro: Pro keeps working even when the license server is unreachable.

blocks.text: After each successful validation, the plugin caches your signed license state locally for 7 days. Scheduled chains, transfers, restores and encryption continue uninterrupted during network partitions, firewalled segments or maintenance windows. The cache renews automatically on the first successful contact, and expiry never disables anything mid-run.

expiration.title: Expiration & Grace Period
expiration.intro: Renewal is predictable, forgiving, and never destructive to your data.

items: Reminder notifications arrive 3 days before expiry — dashboard, email and Central Bot.
A 7-day grace period follows expiry with full functionality.
After grace, Pro features pause; read access to every existing backup — local, cloud and encrypted (with your key) — is preserved indefinitely.
Renewing reactivates everything exactly where it left off, chains and schedules included.

plan-comparison.title: Plan Comparison
plan-comparison.intro: Every Pro capability, sized to four plans — starting with a free 10-day trial.

cli-free.title: Available Commands (Free)
cli-free.intro: The full backup lifecycle is scriptable with WP-CLI — perfect for cron automation and CI/CD pipelines.

blocks.text: wp backupino create

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
wp backupino create
wp backupino create --label="pre-release-v2"

blocks.text: wp backupino create --db-only

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
wp backupino create --db-only
wp backupino create --files-only

blocks.text: wp backupino jobs
Lists running and recent jobs with their stage, progress percentage and checkpoint state — the terminal view of the dashboard's live progress card.

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
wp backupino jobs
# token   status     stage     progress
c92f…   running    files     64%

blocks.text: wp backupino status
Reports installation health: PHP version, required extensions, storage permissions, cron wiring and destination reachability — the same checks as Settings → System Status, in machine-readable form.

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
wp backupino status
# php: 8.2 OK | pdo_mysql OK | zip OK | storage writable OK | cron OK

cli-pro.title: Extended Commands (Pro)
cli-pro.intro: Pro extends the CLI with cloud, scheduling, restore and license verbs — full fleet automation from one terminal.

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.content:
# Cloud destinations
wp backupino cloud test --destination=s3-main
wp backupino cloud push --last

# Scheduling
wp backupino schedule set --interval=hourly --chain=cloud,clean
wp backupino schedule status

# Restore & points
wp backupino restore points
wp backupino restore --chain=abc123 --to=2026-11-01T06:00

# License
wp backupino license status
wp backupino license deactivate

common-issues.title: Common Issues
common-issues.intro: Timeouts, memory exhaustion and permission errors on shared hosting — and how Backupino's engine plus a few settings solve them.

items: 504 / Gateway Timeout — the chunk engine resumes automatically; reduce Batch File Processing from 300 to 100 on constrained hosts.
memory_limit exhaustion — Backupino raises limits during heavy stages with wp_raise_memory_limit('admin'); set memory_limit to 256 MB where possible.
max_allowed_packet SQL errors — the streamer and installer auto-split oversized INSERTs; 64 MB packets are recommended for large sites.
Permission errors — directories 755, files 644; on read-only wp-content, storage automatically falls back to uploads/backupino/.
500 errors during restore — the installer's server-config quarantine (.backupino-orig) eliminates LiteSpeed/cPanel handler conflicts.

server-compat.title: Server Compatibility
server-compat.intro: Notes for specific hosting stacks — verified across cPanel, DirectAdmin, Plesk, LiteSpeed, Nginx, IIS and local environments.

items: cPanel & WHM / DirectAdmin — database prefixes and ALL PRIVILEGES grants are the standard path; LiteSpeed cache directives are quarantined during migration.
Nginx (PHP-FPM) — no .htaccess processing applies; Backupino writes equivalent protection rules for its packages directory.
Microsoft IIS — a dedicated web.config guards archives; restore proceeds identically.
CloudLinux CageFS — isolated LVE limits are respected by the batch engine; raise LVE memory for the smoothest large-site runs.
Local environments (XAMPP, Laragon, LocalWP, Docker) — fully supported for migration testing.

wp-cron.title: WP-Cron Limitations
wp-cron.intro: WordPress cron depends on page views — fine for busy sites, unreliable for quiet ones. Two patterns make schedules deterministic.

blocks.text: Replace traffic-driven cron with a real system cron hitting wp-cron.php, while leaving WordPress's internal scheduler untouched. Backupino's heartbeat endpoint keeps long chains moving between ticks.

blocks.title: Server cron (recommended)
blocks.content:
# wp-config.php
define('DISABLE_WP_CRON', true);

# crontab — every 5 minutes
*/5 * * * * curl -s https://yourdomain.com/wp-cron.php?doing_wp_cron >/dev/null 2>&1

blocks.text: Pro's chained schedules checkpoint between ticks — even a quiet site with infrequent visitors completes hourly chains reliably because each tick only advances a measured slice.

items.q: Does the free version impose size limits or quotas?
items.a: No. No size caps, no file-count limits, no record restrictions — from small sites to massive WooCommerce stores.

items.q: Is restoring or migrating ever charged?
items.a: Never. The standalone installer and migration are 100% free forever in the core plugin.

items.q: Do I need WordPress installed on the destination?

items.q: Does Backupino work with WooCommerce?

items.q: Does anything phone home?

items.q: What happens when a Pro license expires?
items.a: Features pause after a 7-day grace period; read access to every existing backup is preserved.

faq.label: Download FAQs
faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Downloading Backupino
faq.subtitle: Clear answers to the most common inquiries regarding installation, recovery, and licensing.

items.q: Is restoring and migrating sites with the free edition really 100% free?
items.a: Yes, absolutely. Unlike proprietary plugins that let you backup for free but hold restores hostage behind a paywall, Backupino provides unlimited restores and bare-metal migrations with installer.php completely free forever.

items.q: What is standalone installer.php and how does it enable WordPress-free restores?
items.a: installer.php is a self-contained recovery engine. You simply upload your backup ZIP package and installer.php to any clean host directory, open yoursite.com/installer.php in your browser, and it provisions your site from scratch without WordPress pre-installed.

items.q: How does the anti-timeout chunk engine prevent 504 Gateway Timeouts on budget shared hosts?
items.a: Backupino slices backup jobs into adaptive 3 to 5-second micro-chunks. State is safely saved to the database after each chunk, allowing subsequent requests to resume effortlessly without triggering host max_execution_time limits.

items.q: Can I connect Backupino to S3-compatible cloud storage providers?
items.a: Yes. Backupino supports standard S3 API buckets including Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, MinIO, ArvanCloud, and Liara for offsite security.

items.q: Does Backupino affect frontend website speed or search engine rankings?
items.a: No. Backupino is strictly offline-first. It injects zero scripts or fonts onto your public visitor frontend, ensuring your Core Web Vitals and SEO rankings remain pristine.
